water_wagon_records.stands_on: the east bank at the foot of Randolph Street
water_wagon_records.note: A two-wheeled cart with a hogshead mounted, standing at the watering place at the foot of Randolph Street, facing the water on Randolph's own bearing of 90.5 degrees. THE TRADE IS DOCUMENTED AND THIS CART IS NOT: Andreas 1884 (`town_findings_andreas_v1#c013`) attests water carts of exactly this description working this town in the era July 1835 falls inside, and attests the place; that a cart stood here on this morning, and whose it was, is invented, which is why it carries no mark of any kind. Unhitched with its shafts down on the ground, like every other vehicle in this scene — there is no team here and there never will be. docs/LIBERTIES.md L227.
